$comment: The Wayland protocol table: one source of truth for docs/WAYLAND.md's generated table and lordos.org/wayland-protocols-table. Edit the lordos fields by hand; tools/wayland-app-import.mjs refreshes kwin and mutter; tools/gen-wayland-table.mjs writes the outputs; server/tests/wayland_table_test.mjs checks them against server/src/wl.

statuses.supported: lord-server advertises it (to every client, or as the note says).
statuses.partial: Advertised, with part of the protocol left out (the note says which).
statuses.on-purpose: Not offered on purpose: a LordOS decision, with the reason in the note.
statuses.missing: Not offered yet, or not needed; the note says if it is planned.

lordos.note: Created by libwayland's wl_display_init_shm (version 2 since libwayland 1.22; Debian 13 has 1.23).
Deprecated; replaced by xdg-shell.

destroy_registry: a client drops a wl_registry it no longer needs and lord-server stops sending it global events. Debian 13's libwayland is 1.23, so the interface comes from wayland.xml 1.24, vendored. Not yet checked with a real app.
Version 2 (feedback per display) since 0.8.9.5.
Version 7 (constrained_* states) since 0.8.9.5.
Version 5 (one modifier for every plane) since 0.8.9.5.

Pens (pressure, tilt, distance, rotation, slider, buttons) and pads (buttons, rings, strips, dials) read from evdev by LordOS's own tablet.c, without libinput or libwacom. Not the tool's wheel or pad modes beyond one. Not yet checked with a real tablet.

protocols.name: XDG activation
protocols.summary: Protocol for requesting activation of surfaces

lordos.note: Only a connector the kernel marks non-desktop (a VR headset), only to an app the person allowed (the vr permission: Allow once, Always allow, Don't allow), never to a sandboxed or isolated app or Xwayland; revoked on unplug, permission taken back, lock, user switch or text console. Approved by the maintainer 2026-11-22. Not yet checked with a real headset.

A dmabuf frame is applied once its acquire point is signalled, without blocking, and its release point is signalled when LordOS is done with it. Offered when a render node has timeline syncobjs and SYNCOBJ_EVENTFD (Linux 6.6), on the GPU and the CPU path (docs/WAYLAND.md, "Explicit sync").
lordos.checked: build/syncobj-test, tests/syncobj_headless.sh; vkcube (Mesa 25.0.7 Vulkan) on an AMD RX 580

protocols.name: Session lock
protocols.summary: Secure session locking with arbitrary graphics

lordos.note: LordOS locks the screen itself; an outside locker would draw over the session (docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md).
Kept per surface and applied on commit; nothing uses it yet (docs/WAYLAND.md "Frame timing").
lordos.checked: headless lord-server: tests/wltiming_headless.sh, vkcube (lavapipe, and Mesa's Intel driver with explicit sync)

lordos.note: Only once the person allowed the app (the idle permission).

No app copies the screen on its own. It asks through LordOS's ScreenCast portal and gets only what the person picks, while the indicator shows it (docs/FIREWALL.md, docs/WAYLAND.md "Sharing a screen or a window").

No app copies the screen on its own. It asks through LordOS's ScreenCast portal and gets only what the person picks, while the indicator shows it (docs/FIREWALL.md, docs/WAYLAND.md "Sharing a screen or a window").

The hint is kept; "async" tears only a fullscreen app's own buffer scanned out alone, when the driver reports DRM_CAP_ASYNC_PAGE_FLIP; composed frames wait for vblank. The torn flip is not yet checked on hardware (docs/WAYLAND.md "Frame timing").
lordos.checked: headless lord-server: tests/wltiming_headless.sh, vkcube (lavapipe, and Mesa's Intel driver with explicit sync)

protocols.name: Xwayland shell
protocols.summary: Protocol for associating X11 windows to wl_surfaces

lordos.note: lord-server starts Xwayland itself and matches its windows with WL_SURFACE_ID (server/src/wl/xwm.c).

protocols.name: Fractional scale
protocols.summary: Protocol for requesting fractional surface scales

lordos.note: Version 2 (dnd_ask, all_resize) since 0.8.9.5.
A program could list and control other apps' windows (third-party docks and taskbars). LordOS's Dock, switcher and window list are part of the desktop (docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md).
Built; not yet checked on the VM with a real Flatpak.
Only for a trusted desktop tool; if it is ever added, sandboxed clients won't see it (secctx.c's hidden list).
Tab tear-off: the window follows the pointer at the app's offset, is never the drag's target and stays where it is let go.
lordos.checked: Chromium 156 on a headless lord-server (tear-off and reattach); tests/shellx_headless.sh

protocols.name: XDG toplevel icon
protocols.summary: Protocol to assign icons to toplevels

lordos.note: Used only when the app has no installed icon; buffers re-encoded and size-limited, icon names ignored.
An update is not shown before its target on wp_presentation's clock: it applies at the latch of the first frame predicted at or after it (docs/WAYLAND.md "Frame timing").
lordos.checked: headless lord-server: tests/wltiming_headless.sh, vkcube (lavapipe, and Mesa's Intel driver with explicit sync)

lordos.note: A program could read every copy, or replace the clipboard, without having the focus. LordOS gives the clipboard only to the focused app; GNOME doesn't offer it either (docs/DESKTOP-PARITY.md).

An update waits until the surface's display has latched a frame since the one that set the barrier: Mesa's Vulkan FIFO mode runs at the display's rate. Held in explicit sync's queue; hidden windows and a screen that is off clear it once a second (docs/WAYLAND.md "Frame timing").
lordos.checked: headless lord-server: tests/wltiming_headless.sh, vkcube (lavapipe, and Mesa's Intel driver with explicit sync)

lordos.note: LordOS's alert sound (not in Do Not Disturb) and a window not in front marked as wanting attention; at most one ring every 250 ms per app.
Only for a trusted desktop tool; if it is ever added, sandboxed clients won't see it (secctx.c's hidden list).

Parametric descriptions only (no ICC, no luminances or mastering metadata, no scRGB); pixels are converted to the SDR sRGB / gamma 2.2 every display is driven with. No HDR (docs/WAYLAND.md, "Colour management").
Alpha modes premultiplied electrical, premultiplied optical and straight; coefficients and range identity / full only, since lord-server imports no YUV buffer.
A window's tag keys its own remembered place; its description names the window while it has no title.
Only within the app's own surface, with the pointer over it, the serial of its enter and the keyboard; never while the pointer is locked or in a drag. Not yet checked with an app on the VM.
Blur behind a region of a window, drawn with the UI's own backdrop blur: offered only on the CPU path with transparency and blur on, not on the GPU path.
An app's windows come back where they were: random session ids, scoped to the program lord-server checked, kept in ~/.config/lordos/wl-sessions (mode 0600).
An outside input method would read every key. LordOS's own input methods (server/src/ime.c) compose into apps through text-input-v3 (docs/WAYLAND.md, "Input methods").
